checkpoints.root_cause: KeyValueEntry::make('signals') in ViewTaxonomyCandidateConceptLink.php requires flat string=>string values and calls htmlspecialchars() on each raw value. CanonicalConceptApplyService::apply() (line 229) stores signals = ['possible_existing_concepts' => [...]] for PROPOSE_NEW_CONCEPT candidates - a nested array value, not a scalar. PHP 8.2 throws TypeError on htmlspecialchars(array), even for an empty array. All 10 candidates from the Phase C run (ids 263-272) are PROPOSE_NEW_CONCEPT, so all 10 failed identically.

contract_implemented.freeze: ReviewedProposalService::freeze() - congeals a human review decision (MAP_TO_EXISTING/CREATE_NEW/REJECT on a taxonomy_candidate_concept_links row, or PUBLISH_RELATION/REJECT on a taxonomy_concept_relations row) into an immutable taxonomy_reviewed_proposals row with payload_fingerprint (tamper detection) and taxonomy_state_fingerprint (staleness detection, same CanonicalConceptBuilderService::dryRunInputFingerprint() as Phase C1). Never rediscovers or recomputes the proposal - never calls dryRun()/scoredCandidatesForTerm(). Never writes to taxonomy_term_concepts/taxonomy_canonical_concepts/taxonomy_concept_relations. Never touches the source candidate/relation's status.
contract_implemented.apply: ReviewedProposalService::apply(proposalId, authorizationReference) - authorizationReference required, non-empty, must contain a digit (same format convention as CanonicalConceptApplyService::apply()); target_environment auto-captured via app()->environment(), never caller-supplied. Inside one DB transaction: lockForUpdate() the payload row (idempotent replay if already APPLIED/ABORTED, no new writes), recompute and compare payload_fingerprint (tamper), recompute and compare taxonomy_state_fingerprint (staleness), lockForUpdate() and re-verify the real candidate/relation entity's current status (server-side, independent of the frozen payload), re-run validateConceptRelationProposal() with excludeId for PUBLISH_RELATION (same mechanism as TASK-0003 finding 6), only then write and mark the payload APPLIED - or write an explicit ABORTED status with a specific reason if any check fails. Every apply()/abort() outcome is audited via TaxonomyAuditLogger with authorization_reference/target_environment populated (actor_type=system) - distinct from freeze()'s review-time audit entry, which deliberately has neither field populated (actor_type=user).
contract_implemented.idempotency_mechanism: DB-enforced, not check-then-act: two partial unique indexes (taxonomy_reviewed_proposals_one_pending_per_candidate / _relation, WHERE status='PENDING_APPLY') via insertOrIgnore() block concurrent double-freeze of the same candidate/relation; lockForUpdate() + status re-check inside apply()'s transaction blocks double-apply (a second apply() of an already-APPLIED payload returns ALREADY_APPLIED with zero new writes, verified by test asserting audit_log row count is unchanged after a replay).
contract_implemented.not_implemented: No Filament UI wiring for a reviewer to trigger freeze() from the panel - out of scope for this task's requested execution mode (DESIGN + IMPLEMENT + TEST, no UI mandate). freeze()/apply() are invocable today via service call, tinker, or the new taxonomy:apply-reviewed-proposal artisan command (apply() only).

Process note (self-caught bug 1): the initial tamper-detection fingerprint used reviewed_at formatted with microsecond precision on both the freeze-time and apply-time sides, but Laravel's query builder binds a DateTime to Postgres using the grammar's date format, which does not preserve microseconds - so every apply(), even an untouched one, failed as a false-positive TAMPER_DETECTED. Caught by the first, simplest test failing unexpectedly; fixed by using second precision (matching what actually round-trips) on both sides.

Process note (self-caught bug 2): one test (the relation-revalidation abort scenario) created its 'waiting for review' relation row before its 'already approved symmetric duplicate' row - the reverse of the order TaxonomyConceptRelationValidationTest (TASK-0003) already documented as required, because TaxonomyConceptRelation::booted()'s guard checks for a symmetric duplicate regardless of the other row's status. This made the guard fire during the test's own fixture setup instead of during apply()'s intended revalidation. Fixed by swapping the creation order, mirroring the precedent already established in the approved suite.
